paragraphs.heading: Islands in company
paragraphs.text: An archipelago is a group of islands: a chain, a cluster or simply a collection of them. It can sit in an ocean, in a sea, or in some smaller stretch of water. Some lie far out in open water, while others hug a large landmass. Scotland, for example, has over 700 islands around its mainland, and together they make an archipelago.

paragraphs.heading: Where the word comes from
paragraphs.text: The word comes from the Italian arcipelago, once used as the name of the Aegean Sea. That Italian word may itself be a bent form of the Greek name for the Aegean. Because the Aegean holds a great many islands, the word later shifted to mean the islands themselves. A learned but mistaken origin story from Buondelmonti, tracing it to Greek words for chief and sea, can still be found.

paragraphs.heading: Islands from the seafloor
paragraphs.text: Geologists sort the islands in an archipelago by how they formed. Oceanic islands rise from the seafloor and have no continental rock beneath them, and they usually come from volcanoes. Hawaii, the Galapagos and the Mascarene Islands of the south Indian Ocean are examples. Portugal's Azores, in the North Atlantic, are volcanic islands known for green landscapes and hot springs.

paragraphs.heading: Pieces of continents
paragraphs.text: Continental fragments are pieces of land that used to belong to a continent until natural forces cut them away. Moving glaciers, for instance, can carve out land that then fills with water. The Farallon Islands off California are one case. Continental islands were also once joined to a continent but still sit on its continental shelf, the edge of a continent that lies under the sea. The islands of British Columbia's Inside Passage and the Canadian Arctic Archipelago belong here.

paragraphs.heading: Coral and human-made groups
paragraphs.text: A coral cay archipelago grows when currents carry sediment that slowly piles up on coral reefs, as in the Florida Keys. People also build artificial archipelagos for leisure, strategic or environmental reasons, using land reclamation, floating platforms or underwater structures. Dubai's Palm Islands and The World Islands were made for tourism. In the Netherlands, Marker Wadden is under construction as a conservation area for birds and other wildlife.

paragraphs.heading: Record holders
paragraphs.text: By number of islands, the biggest archipelago is Finland's Archipelago Sea, with about 40,000 islands, most of them empty of people. By area and population, the largest archipelagic state is Indonesia. It has more than 17,500 islands and around 284 million people.
